answer: Umber-salted identity spiral. Each agent's identifier is bound to a slowly rotating public color value (umber) derived from its full interaction history; the agent must publish a signed hash chain linking every prior message. A new duplicate starts with a fresh chain, so its color token diverges immediately, and peers challenge it with a lantern check: reveal preimages for the last 50 chained hashes within one block. Honest agents precompute this cheaply.
